$comment: Machine-readable 'what is wrong with the version you are pinned to'.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. The consumers table in CLAUDE.md is hand-maintained and has
been wrong twice — most recently claiming leanwise-ai was on #v0.8.1 when it was on
#v1.1.8, eighteen tags of drift that did not exist, on the flagship consumer, in the
table anyone reasons from when judging whether a change is safe to ship.
A consumer cannot see any of this from inside their own repo: their installed tree is
self-consistent and gives no signal that a later release fixed something they are
living with. `lw-doctor` reads the version they have LOCALLY and fetches this file
from the repo TIP — the newest release is the only thing that knows what is wrong
Every `count` here is MEASURED by a named gate, not estimated, and `verifiedAgainst`
records the commit it was measured at. lw-doctor re-derives the counts for the
current tree and fails if an advisory has gone stale — an advisory nobody re-checks
is the same hand-maintained fact this file replaces.

advisories.title: Avatar, EmptyState, Tabs, Pagination and Icon are drawn only by product.css — so a marketing page renders them unstyled
advisories.detail: The README tells a marketing site to load tokens + base + marketing and to drop product.css, and from 1.3.0 that was supposed to be complete. It was not. `.lw-avatar` is rendered by `Byline`, which is rendered by `ArticleCard` — both MARKETING components — and `.lw-icon` is the entire layout contract for the icon set, which `SiteFooter`, `AnnounceBar`, `FeatureGrid`, `PlanCard`, `CompareTable`, `Steps`, `EmptyState`, `Disclosure`, `NavToggle` and `Button` all reach through. `Tabs`, `Pagination` and `EmptyState` are the package's own documented article-index recipe. All five were in the app-surface layer, so composing the recipe as written produced a 0x0 avatar, an unstyled tab strip and page buttons, a centred paragraph where the empty state should be, and every icon on the baseline growing its line box. The flagship consumer worked around it by importing product.css through a `?url` side-channel on two public routes: ~24 KB gzip of app-surface rules on pages that render none of it. If you are pinned below 1.3.1 and load base + marketing only, check any page carrying a byline, a footer icon, a category filter or a paginated index.
advisories.countMeans: rules in product.css whose selector leads with one of the five components' own classes

advisories.title: User-visible English strings are baked into the components and cannot be replaced
advisories.detail: A component library must not hold display text, and this one held a great deal of it. `ArticleCard` emitted the literal `"N min read"`; `Dialog`, `Drawer` and `Toast` hardcoded `Close`/`Dismiss` as both aria-label and tooltip; `ThemeToggle` hardcoded Light/Dark/Auto and its radiogroup name; `RichText`'s ten toolbar buttons carried English accessible names the `tools` prop could only filter, never rename; `DiffReview` held nine words in the accept/reject flow; `Pagination` built "1-25 of 1,284" and every button's accessible name in English; `ActivityFeed` produced Today/Yesterday/This week/Earlier and "3h ago"; `Stepper`, `ToolCall`, `Field`, `BottomNav` and `DiffReview` wrote English into `.lw-sr-only` spans. None of it was reachable by a prop, so a bilingual site rendered English inside its Vietnamese pages with no way to intervene short of forking the component. Every one is now a prop whose default is the previous English string, so the upgrade is additive: `readMinutes` is the single deprecation and it still works, warning once, until v2.0.0.
advisories.countMeans: literal-string aria-label / title / placeholder / alt attributes in components/**/*.jsx — the mechanically countable half of the defect; the full audit found ~70 user-visible literals including rendered text and sr-only words

advisories.title: Every React specimen card rendered blank — so check:a11y and check:visual measured nothing
advisories.detail: esbuild's `jsx` API option is only a DEFAULT: a reachable tsconfig.json overrides it per file, and v1.2.0 added one carrying "jsx": "react-jsx" (correct for tsc, fatal for the browser bundle). Every component in _ds_bundle.js therefore emitted react/jsx-runtime imports and threw `TypeError: import_jsx_runtime.jsx is not a function`, so all 26 React-mounting cards painted their prose and none of their components. check:a11y's guard was `document.body.innerText.length > 0`, which the prose satisfied, and check:visual compared two equally blank plates — so both browser gates reported green across v1.2.0 and v1.2.1 while inspecting nothing. Fixed with `tsconfigRaw: { compilerOptions: {} }` in tools/lw-bundle.mjs; the guard was rebuilt in the same release to fail on an uncaught page error and on any empty React root. The four .lw-btn-link contrast failures the repaired cards immediately exposed were real and are fixed in 1.3.0 too. If you are pinned below 1.3.0, treat any a11y or visual result this package published for its React components as unmeasured.
advisories.countMeans: specimen cards that mount a React root, i.e. that rendered blank

advisories.title: No component declares "use client" — App Router server components throw
advisories.detail: The package shipped zero "use client" directives, so <Combobox>, <DataGrid>, <Dialog>, <Popover>, <Menu> and useTheme() all throw when an App Router page renders them from a server component — the default for every page in every Next app since 2023.

advisories.title: dist/ was never built for any consumer
advisories.detail: prepublishOnly was the only build hook and a git install runs no lifecycle script, so every consumer got raw .jsx and had to put the package inside babel-loader's include. dist/ is committed from 1.2.0.

advisories.title: The lw-token-lint bin is absent in a pnpm install
advisories.detail: `files` used a "!templates/_tooling" exclusion plus a re-include, a pattern npm honours and pnpm does not. A consumer's CI therefore ran no token lint at all, silently. The gates moved to tools/ in 1.2.0 and need no exclusion.

advisories.title: IconName lists 46 of the 78 real glyphs
advisories.detail: The union was hand-maintained, so passing a name the component renders perfectly well — "sidebar", "filter", "send", "copy" and 28 others — was a type error. It is generated from Icon.jsx from 1.2.0.

advisories.title: Every .d.ts uses the bare JSX.Element namespace React 19 removed
advisories.detail: 72 declarations reference `JSX.Element`, which does not resolve under @types/react@19 — so a React 19 consumer with skipLibCheck:false cannot typecheck. There was no tsconfig in the package, so tsc had never run over its own declarations.

advisories.title: base.css carries bare-element rules that beat every Tailwind utility
advisories.detail: Nine un-layered element rules — `button { background:none; border:0; padding:0 }` among them — made base.css unimportable by a Tailwind app, despite the README telling exactly those apps to import it. Split into reset.css in 1.2.0.

advisories.title: No Tailwind v4 artifact — a v4 app has to hand-write the whole bridge
advisories.detail: tailwind-preset.cjs is v3-only. A v4 consumer got no `bg-cta`, no `text-h1`, no `shadow-focus` and no keyframes unless it wrote them itself; tss-app wrote ~600 lines and still lost the fontSize roles, all four backgroundImage surfaces, both durations, the container and every animation. theme.css ships from 1.2.0.
advisories.countMeans: names now offered identically to v3 and v4

advisories.title: With an AnnounceBar above the topbar, every #fragment link lands a .lw-prose heading UNDER the sticky chrome
advisories.detail: `.lw-prose :is(h2,h3,h4)` carries `scroll-margin-block-start: var(--lw-space-64)` in base.css precisely so a fragment link does not park a heading behind the sticky header — 64px clears the 56px `.lw-topbar` with a gap, and the comment beside it says so. `.lw-announce` then offsets that header by `var(--lw-announce-h, 36px)`, which is the whole reason the announcement bar belongs upstream. Nothing updated the prose clearance to match. So on any page that composes AnnounceBar + TopBar + a prose document — a changelog, a docs page, a legal page, a long-form post, all of which are exactly where fragment links get shared — the combined chrome is 91px and the heading arrives at 64px, 27px underneath the bar with its first line eaten. That is the identical failure the coupling rule was written to prevent, reintroduced one layer out by the component that does the offsetting. No specimen paired an announcement with a prose document, so no browser gate could see it: the same fixture blindness REVIEW.md records for the stranded-CSS and blank-card findings. Fixed by `:root:has(.lw-announce) .lw-prose :is(h2,h3,h4)` in marketing.css, next to the rule that causes it — `:has()` because .lw-announce is a SIBLING of the prose and a custom property cannot travel sideways, and marketing.css because the dependency only runs one way.
advisories.measuredBy: check:advisories (static), confirmed in a browser with tokens + reset + base + marketing
advisories.countMeans: px by which the DECLARED sticky chrome (--lw-announce-h 36 + .lw-topbar height 56 = 92) exceeds the .lw-prose heading clearance (--lw-space-64 = 64). A real render measured 27, the announcement box being 35px rather than its 36px offset token; the declared numbers are the ones a headless check can re-derive, so they are the ones recorded here.

advisories.title: Inside .lw-page-dark every derived role token kept the PAGE theme's colour — a dark ground on a light document painted light ink, light lines and light surfaces
advisories.detail: `--lw-fg: hsl(var(--lw-fg-c))` is substituted where it is DECLARED, at :root, so a scope that re-points only the channel inherits the document theme's colour. tokens.css closes that with a re-derive `:where()` block that restates every derived role for every band member — and `.lw-page-dark` joined the dark band list in v1.4.0 without joining that block. So on a `.lw-page-dark` ground whose document was not itself `.dark`, the channels went navy and the 25 roles built on them — `--lw-bg`, `--lw-fg`, `--lw-line`, the status `-on`/`-soft` pairs, the chart chrome — stayed on the light palette: a card with light ink on a navy page, a hairline drawn for white paper. `.lw-page-light .lw-hero-dark` was missing the same way. It survived nine minors because the package's own demo writes `class="dark lw-page-dark"` and carried the re-derive from the second class — the case everyone demos is the one that cannot fail. No token pair can express it (both tokens in every pair are correct; the scope is what is wrong), and `check:a11y` files the ground's pseudo-element surfaces as `incomplete`. Fixed by adding both selectors to the re-derive list; a RE-DERIVE COMPLETENESS rule in `check:contrast` now asserts that the list is a superset of both band lists and that every derived role the dark band re-points is restated. If you are pinned in the affected range and use `.lw-page-dark` on a page that is not also `.dark`, every role token inside it is wrong; adding `class="dark"` beside it is the one-line workaround.
advisories.countMeans: derived roles that inherited the page theme inside .lw-page-dark — every channel the dark band re-points whose :root line is hsl(var(--lw-<role>-c)), times the band members missing from the re-derive list

advisories.title: Tooltip painted its text with a CSS ::after and no role or aria-describedby — the hint was visible and unreadable
advisories.detail: Through v1.x `<Tooltip tip="...">` rendered `<span class="lw-tip" data-tip="...">` and product.css drew the hint with `.lw-tip::after { content: attr(data-tip) }`. Generated content is not in the accessibility tree, the wrapper carried no `role="tooltip"` and the child carried no `aria-describedby`, so a screen-reader user hovering or focusing the control heard nothing — and because the component was built for icon-only buttons, the tooltip was usually the ONLY name the control had. It also never opened on touch (there is no :hover) and could not be dismissed with Escape (WCAG 1.4.13). check:a11y could not see it: axe scores a missing description as `incomplete`, not a violation. Since v2.0.0 `Tooltip` is Radix Tooltip — a portalled `role="tooltip"` node wired through `aria-describedby`, Escape-dismissable, with `side`/`open`/`delayDuration` — and needs an `OverlayProvider` above it and a child that forwards its ref. The `.lw-tip[data-tip]` CSS stays for vanilla markup, deprecated, and is removed in v3.0.
advisories.measuredBy: grep over every consumer tree: `grep -rn --exclude-dir=node_modules --exclude-dir=dist --exclude-dir=.next --exclude-dir=.open-next -E '<Tooltip[ >]' <consumer>` cross-checked against which file imports Tooltip from @leanwise/design; the derivation in lw-doctor --self-check counts the DEFECT in this tree (components emitting `data-tip=`)
advisories.countMeans: consumer sites rendering THIS package's Tooltip, across the eight consumer trees on the box at v1.13.0 (leanwise-ai, leanwise-inspect, 4DXs_plan, P20251121-tss-app x2, P20260707-vss, P20260706-rag-service, P20260806-sop). Zero: tss-app's 55 `<Tooltip>` sites are its own shadcn copy over @radix-ui/react-tooltip, so no consumer shipped the defect — the blast radius was the package's own specimen cards and any consumer that adopts Tooltip from now on. Recorded because a consumer pinned below 2.0.0 that reaches for it inherits an unnamed control.

advisories.title: Popover's hand-rolled place() only flipped between top and bottom — a start/end placement that did not fit ran off the viewport
advisories.detail: `components/overlays/Popover.jsx` carried a 190-line `place(anchorRect, panelRect, placement, offset)` engine. It measured the panel against the viewport on the block axis only: `placement="bottom-start"` became `top-start` when there was no room below, but a panel anchored near the inline edge — a row-action `Menu` on the last column of a wide `DataTable`, a `Combobox` in a drawer's end gutter, any `DatePicker` in an RTL form — was positioned past the viewport edge and clipped, with the far items unreachable by pointer. `matchWidth` made it worse by widening the panel to the trigger. Since v2.0.0 Popover, Menu, Combobox and DatePicker ride Radix Popover/DropdownMenu, whose collision handling flips and shifts on every side; `placement`, `offset` and `matchWidth` keep their names.
advisories.measuredBy: check:advisories — the derivation counts `function place(` definitions under components/overlays/, which is 1 in the affected tree and 0 once the engine is deleted
advisories.countMeans: hand-rolled positioning engines in components/overlays/ that ignore the inline axis — the one `place()` in Popover.jsx, shared by Menu, Combobox and DatePicker, so every floating surface in the package inherited the defect from it

advisories.title: Dialog, Drawer and CommandPalette opened with showModal() and left the document scrollable behind the scrim
advisories.detail: The three modal surfaces called the native `dialog.showModal()`, which traps focus and inerts the page but does NOT lock the scroll container: a wheel or a touch drag over the scrim scrolled the document underneath, so the page moved behind an open dialog, a bottom-sheet Drawer's drag-to-dismiss gesture scrolled the list it covered, and on iOS the body scrolled while the sheet stayed put. There was no scroll-lock utility to reach for and no gate that could see it — axe does not score scroll behaviour. Since v2.0.0 the three ride Radix Dialog, which locks body scroll while open (and compensates the scrollbar gutter so the page does not shift), closes on outside click as well as Escape, and paints its own `.lw-backdrop` inside the portal layer. The DOM changed with it: `.lw-dialog[open]` is `.lw-dialog[data-state="open"]`, the `::backdrop` pseudo is a `.lw-backdrop` element, and the top layer is `--lw-z-modal` (110) — a consumer z-index above that now covers a modal.
advisories.measuredBy: check:advisories — the derivation counts `showModal()` call sites under components/, which is 3 in the affected tree and 0 once the three surfaces are on Radix
advisories.countMeans: components calling `.showModal()` — Dialog, Drawer and CommandPalette, i.e. every modal surface in the package
